reason: Concordia's published honour roll for the A. Ross Seaman Leadership Development Fund names every bursary winner from 1989 to 2006 and describes each one's character, career and camp service in a paragraph. Twenty-seven of those citations mention Kanawana. The people are living private individuals, most of them students at the time, the youngest awarded within twenty years of this reading. The material is laudatory and the university published it, so nothing is being protected from disclosure; what is avoided is this wiki assembling a searchable biography of a private person out of an honour roll. The institutional finding -- that Kanawana was a standing feeder community for the fund across nearly two decades -- is written into wiki/people/a-ross-seaman.md in full, without names. Two individual details are kept without names because their subjects are Seaman and a camp tradition: a Human Relations Award winner's testimony that she 'caught the leadership bug early in her professional career as a camp nurse, under the mentorship of Ross Seaman', and a Capitaine selection for the L&V games by a man at camp from the summer of 1992.
embargo_basis: living private individuals under CLAUDE.md Phase 2 section 7; not a personal assessment, so the 75/100-year default does not apply. review_on is set at record date + ~29 years, by which point the youngest winners are past sixty.
note: AN EMBARGO BLOCK AS OF 2026-09-07; it was not one before, and the change is the point of this note. The original decision was to SUMMARISE the roster rather than write it down, recorded here so a later pass could tell a silent source from a silent editor. That was the weaker treatment under kb/restricted/README.md's own reasoning -- the register knew what was missing, but the article did not, and the record was not whole. It was left standing while p_483 was open, because the repository turned out to be PUBLIC and transcribing the names would have enlarged that problem rather than fixed a filing one. The operator settled p_483 the same day by choosing to leave the repository public with its material in it, which unblocked this: the fourteen Kanawana-connected citations are now transcribed in wiki/people/a-ross-seaman.md inside <!-- embargo:r_0006 --> markers. WHAT IS STILL MISSING and is a scan problem, not a decision: several surnames are set in a script face overlapping a KANAWANA wordmark and did not survive the OCR. Where the transcription gives a first name only, the page images are what is needed.

locator.section: CHARTER ROLL / THE GRAND COMPANY OF THE VOYAGEURS OF VERENDRYE

reason: The charter roll of the 1959 founding company of Les Voyageurs de la Verendrye: thirty boys aged fourteen to seventeen, in six outfits of five, printed by the Montreal YMCA in its own 1960 promotional brochure. It is labelled because the standing instruction in CLAUDE.md Phase 2 section 7 is not to publish personal information about living private individuals, and thirty names with an age band is that; these men would now be in their eighties. The aggregate is carried unembargoed in f_5482 and stated openly in the article, and the three leaders are named outside the block as staff.

The review date is set deliberately later, at 2060-01-01, to match the comparable roster at r_0007 so the two are looked at together -- nothing is lost by reviewing material that is written down and safe a second time, and a split review date would mean whoever opens the register in 2042 has to reason about this all over again.
release_conditions: Consent of an individual, or confirmed death, releases that individual's row earlier. A reviewer may reasonably conclude that a founding roll printed by the organisation itself for public reading never needed labelling at all; the material is here for that judgement to be made.

locator.section: human-interest profile immediately following the chairman's and president's message

reason: A promotional profile in the association's own 2007 annual report, telling the story of a Pathfinders canoe expedition of about 2004 -- nine girl campers, several days on the river, a storm -- and naming two people: a camper who was THIRTEEN at the expedition and almost sixteen when the report appeared, and her section counsellor, who was SEVENTEEN and twenty. Both would be in their thirties now. The institutional content is valuable and is carried in full and UNRESTRICTED in wiki/history/coeducation-gender.md: the camp ran multi-day river trips for girls alone inside a coeducational camp, and the counsellor's stated reason -- 'a l'abri du regard des garcons', out of the boys' gaze -- is the only rationale for single-sex programming this project holds from someone delivering it. WHAT IS WITHHELD IS THE TWO NAMES AND NOTHING ELSE.

release_conditions: Consent of the individuals, or confirmed death. Note that release here would mean transcribing the names into the wiki for the first time, not lifting a marker: they were never carried across.
note: THIS DEPARTS FROM r_0008 AND THE DEPARTURE IS DELIBERATE. r_0008 labelled a roster of named minors from a public 1959 brochure and wrote the names into the article inside an embargo block. That was a reasonable trade for people now in their eighties. It is not the same case: these two are living and in their thirties, and the subject is a child's moment of distress on a canoe trip. This directory's own README records that the repository is PUBLIC and that an embargo marker is an HTML comment which renders as ordinary prose on github.com -- so the block provides LABELLING, NOT PROTECTION. Where the subject is a contemporary private individual who was a child, labelling is not enough and the names are simply not carried across. AND IT IS NOT AN INVISIBLE HOLE: the withholding is stated in the article itself, with the source, the locator and this register id, so a reader can see exactly what was withheld and reach it in one step.
